transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I've called this meeting because we have a situation that needs our attention. The boiler serving the early-childhood wing requires repair, and one of our classrooms will need to operate elsewhere for ten school days beginning January 8. The affected classroom serves 20 students and has its own tables, nap mats, and teaching materials. I've reviewed a draft relocation plan that places the class in Room B204, keeps medication handling under the regular classroom routine, uses the standard furniture arrangement, and serves lunch in the classroom. Before I can sign off on this plan, our relocation procedure requires a routine check-in with facilities, the nurse, special education, and food service. So I'd like to hear from each of you on whether the draft plan works from your area's perspective, or if there are any concerns we need to address.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to raise a concern about Room B204. My facilities inspection found that Room B204 cannot be used for an early-childhood class during the repair because its required egress door will be blocked by the repair staging. I did confirm with the custodian this morning that the Library has the necessary clearance and available floor area for this class, though I should note the room-status board hasn't been updated yet to reflect that.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a medication concern. My health-plan review shows that one student in the affected classroom needs refrigerated medication kept in the nurse's office, with a nurse check at exactly 10:00 a.m. each relocation day. I verified this plan with the student's family this week, but I have not yet added this instruction to the classroom relocation draft. We need to make sure this 10:00 a.m. nurse check is documented in the plan before it's signed.

We need to make sure the relocation plan includes this accommodation before it's signed.
